Salt of the Earth - 5 Day Itinerary

Day 1 - Santa Cruz + Sucre

We landed in Santa Cruz and took the half-hour flight to Sucre. We did precious little besides grabbing a meal near the Sucre bus terminal. If you haven’t carried them already, be sure to use your time in Sucre to purchase altitude sickness medications.

Buses to Uyuni typically depart from the terminal at 9:00 PM. Be sure to reach a little early as there are several gates.

Day 2 - Uyuni

The overnight bus reached Uyuni shortly before dawn. Day two in Bolivia was also spent uneventfully as we took the time to acclimate to the altitude. Even after medications, be prepared for throbbing headaches and / or light-headedness.

Uyuni is quaint and visibly Andean; both in people and landscape. We said Bolivia is the most indigenous of South American nations, and Uyuni in particular feels almost pre-Columbian.

We hadn’t pre-booked our salt flat tour, so did so with Andes Salt Expeditions.

Day 3 - Uyuni Salt Flats

Finally, on day three, something happens.

We chose to the one-day tour of the salt flats. The three-day tour, which includes Laguna Colorada, is more popular but involves long hours in a vehicle.

Now about the salt flats… we know this blog has called a lot of experiences “surreal”, but the salt flats are very near the top of the surrealist totem pole.

While the vast, blindingly white expanse looks ethereal to say the least, but we got absurdly lucky with some residual water that created the famous mirror effect.

The cactus islands, notably Incahuasi, is arguably the most picturesque sight we have seen. It’s like a Salvador Dali painting come to life!

Unfortunately for us, it was a full moon night, else we had ideas of returning to the flats to look at the stars.

Day 4 - Uyuni

To insure against altitude sickness, we had booked another day in Uyuni. There wasn’t much else to do besides walk around the few blocks of town and pick up souvenirs.

In the evening, we took a bus back to Sucre.

Day 5 - Sucre + Santa Cruz

From Sucre, it was back to Santa Cruz by flight. We had a day in Santa Cruz, but chose to only visit a mall near the airport. If you feel more adventurous, Plaza 24 de Septiembre, the cathedral and Mercado Los Pozos are the top attractions in Santa Cruz.
